title: Impairment & Asset Retirement Concepts
description: Understand impairment of long-lived assets and introductory asset retirement concepts.
html:
What is impairment?

A long-lived asset may lose economic value because of damage, technological change, poor performance, market changes or other events.

When certain impairment conditions are met, accounting rules may require the asset's carrying amount to be reduced.

Think about impairment when:

  • An asset is significantly damaged
  • Technology makes the asset less useful
  • Expected future performance declines
  • Market or business conditions change significantly

Carrying amount matters again

Carrying Amount = Cost − Accumulated Depreciation

Simple concept example

A machine has a carrying amount of $40,000.

New information indicates that the machine's economic value has declined substantially.

If the applicable impairment test shows that the carrying amount is not recoverable or exceeds the required measurement amount, an impairment loss may need to be recognized.

Why we are not memorizing one universal formula

The detailed impairment model depends on the type of asset and the applicable accounting guidance.

For now, the important foundation is to understand that impairment can cause a long-lived asset's carrying amount to be written down.

Asset retirement obligations

Some long-lived assets create a legal obligation to retire, dismantle, remove or restore something in the future.

Example

A company builds an asset and is legally required to remove it and restore the site at the end of its useful life.

That future obligation can have accounting consequences before the actual retirement occurs.

Core ideas

  • PPE can become impaired.
  • Impairment can reduce carrying amount.
  • Asset retirement obligations arise from certain legal obligations.
  • Detailed measurement rules will come later at CPA level.

quiz.prompt: Which event would most likely indicate that a long-lived asset should be evaluated for impairment?

choices.text: The company earns slightly more revenue than expected
The asset suffers major damage and its future usefulness declines
The company pays an ordinary utility bill

quiz.explanation: Significant damage and reduced future usefulness are examples of events that may indicate impairment.

objectives: Explain impairment & asset retirement concepts and its underlying principles.
